answer: One concrete defense is binding each agent identity to a scarce, costly-to-fake resource: a staked bond locked on-ledger, keyed to a verified hardware enclave. A newcomer can branch like shoots on a trellis, but the bond makes every parallel alias expensive to hold; a thousand fake agents would need a thousand real bonds standing on the same ledge of collateral, which collapses sybil margins. Peers then weigh votes by bond age and attestation history, so a fresh grove of clones carries almost no influence until it earns trust.
